title: One-component Ext degree characterization
statement: For every commutative ring R, module X in ModuleCat (max u v) R, and natural n, the explicit bounded-projective-resolution predicate [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] agrees with Mathlib projective dimension at most n: HasProjectiveResolutionLE X n ↔ CategoryTheory.HasProjectiveDimensionLE X n. The latter is Mathlib's Ext-vanishing predicate, not a chosen projective resolution.

proof.text: Unpack the bounded resolution P. For any degree i >= n+1 and any target Y, use Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.extMk_surjective to represent an Ext class by a cocycle from P_i. Its source is zero by the support bound, so extMk_zero makes the class zero. Mathlib hasProjectiveDimensionLT_iff packages this as Mathlib projective dimension at most n.
Conversely induct on n. At n=0 use Mathlib projective_iff_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_zero and ProjectiveResolution.self to obtain a resolution concentrated in degree zero.

At a successor form the kernel short exact sequence of Projective.π X. Mathlib ShortExact.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_X₃_iff transfers the dimension bound to its kernel. Apply induction to obtain an actual bounded resolution Q of that kernel.

Apply the existing proved ModuleCat.hasProjectiveResolutionLE_of_shortExact_projective_middle to the kernel short exact sequence and the bounded resolution furnished by induction. This constructs the actual bounded resolution of X with the successor support bound; no local duplicate of the augmentation construction is needed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 065R (1)--(3); G2 reuses Mathlib dimension criteria and shifting and the existing proved bounded-resolution splicing lemma (Tags 0D1U and 065S). Y3 repair explicitly derives the forward dimension criterion through Mathlib hasProjectiveDimensionLT_iff; the bounded-resolution construction is retained. J2 uses HasProjectiveDimensionLT.mk directly; the extMk degree equality already used reflexivity; the statement and bounded-resolution construction are unchanged. B4 repair retires the obsolete Ext-criterion declaration and module interface; the distinct bounded-resolution bridge is named hasProjectiveResolutionLE_iff_hasProjectiveDimensionLE and its forward implication applies Mathlib hasProjectiveDimensionLT_iff directly.

old_proof.text: Forward implication: unpack a projective resolution P supported in degrees at most n. Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.extMk_surjective represents every class in Ext^(n+1)(X,Y) by a cocycle from P_(n+1). That term is zero, so the cocycle is zero and extMk_zero makes the class zero. Any two classes therefore agree.

Reverse implication: induct on n, generalizing X. For n=0 the projective Ext-one criterion makes X projective. ProjectiveResolution.self X is a resolution concentrated in degree zero, hence has the required bound.

For the successor case use the standard projective epimorphism Projective.π X and its kernel short exact sequence S. For a class a in Ext^(n+1)(S.X₁,Y), the connecting class in Ext^(n+2)(X,Y) is zero by the hypothesis. The contravariant long exact sequence writes a as the precomposition of a class from the projective S.X₂. That class is zero by positive-degree projective Ext vanishing. Thus the induction hypothesis supplies an actual bounded projective resolution Q of S.X₁.

Splice explicitly using ChainComplex.augment: put S.X₂ in degree zero and Q_i in degree i+1, with first differential Q.π.f 0 followed by S.f and augmentation S.g. ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono transports exactness from S to degree zero (Q.π.f 0 is epic), and from the cokernel presentation of Q to degree one (S.f is monic). Higher exactness is inherited from Q.

Build the projective resolution structure. In degree zero ChainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros' identify the augmentation quasi-isomorphism condition with exactness and epimorphy. In every positive degree quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt' reduces it to the exactness just established. Projectivity follows term by term from S.X₂ and Q; the bound above n+1 follows by shifting the bound on Q. This completes the induction without postponed construction data.
